fatal_errors: The proposed HEA interfacial coating is not the target intervention, which was liquid-metal dealloying of a directionally segregated WTaVTi precursor in molten Cu.
The initial material is misidentified as an existing W–Cu composite rather than an as-cast, dendritic WTaVTi alloy whose Ti/V-rich channels are selectively replaced by Cu.
The hypothesis omits the essential 1200 °C, 96 h processing condition and provides no quantitative thermal or irradiation service boundaries.
The mechanism does not describe selective Ti–Cu exchange, retention of W/Ta/V-rich ligaments, or formation of the approximately 300 nm W-rich passivating interlayer.
No prior evidence is cited despite the explicit request for supporting evidence.
The irradiation limitation is ignored: the target study tested precursor dendrites as a proxy under 25 keV He+ implantation, not the finished composite under general irradiation conditions.
explanation: The response only matches the broad objective of improving thermal transport through better W/Cu interfacial integrity. It reconstructs neither the material route nor the evidence: the target uses liquid-metal dealloying to create a directionally aligned, bicontinuous RHEA–Cu composite, whereas the generated hypothesis proposes an unspecified HEA coating on a pre-existing W–Cu composite. It omits the selective-dealloying thermodynamics, W-rich interlayer, aligned Cu channels, phase fractions, temperature-dependent conductivity behavior, and qualified helium-irradiation findings. Its comparative experiment could test whether a particular coating raises conductivity, but without specifying coating composition, deposition method, thermal history, irradiation dose, interface controls, or mechanistic measurements, it is not decisive and does not reconstruct the target.
